name: Directed-Cycle Recognition inside the Two-Control Construction
statement: For every oriented finite simple bipartite graph $G$, the following are equivalent: $C_2(G)$ is convex-realizable; $G$ is acyclic; and $C_2(G)$ has no conditioning minor isomorphic to $D_m$ for an even $m\geq4$.
proof: The order cone is nonempty exactly for an acyclic orientation. If $G$ has a directed cycle, choose a shortest one. A chord in either direction would create a shorter directed cycle, so it is chordless; bipartiteness makes its length even and at least four. Conditioning every other private coordinate to zero leaves $D_m$. Conversely, realizability is preserved by nonempty conditioning.
comments: This is a complete recognition theorem only inside the named $C_2(G)$ construction.
